title: Troubleshooting computer problems
text:
Via aniMotum:

There can be issues getting compilers to work properly, especially on M1 Macs. Often, this is due to missing or incorrect Xcode Command Line Tools and/or Fortran compiler. If you encounter install and compile issues, you may find a solution in the excellent documentation here glmmTMB.

Another good resource for aniMotum-specific technical problems is the ‘Issues’ page of the GitHub repo. For more information on installing this package, please refer to the installation instructions from the README on the aniMotum website.

title: Modelling for movement and spatial ecology with animal telemetry data
text:
Workshop goals

Build regional capacity in modern animal movement modelling
Bridge ecological theory with quantitative and statistical modelling approaches
Introduce contemporary frameworks for analysing movement, behaviour, habitat selection and space use
Develop practical skills in reproducible R-based telemetry workflows
Extract environmental data from static and/or time-matched dynamic layers
Explore emerging approaches in Bayesian modelling and machine learning for movement ecology
Connect movement analyses to conservation planning and management applications
Foster collaboration among students, researchers, conservation practitioners, NGOs, and wildlife managers

title: Modelling for movement and spatial ecology with animal telemetry data
section: Who is this workshop aimed at?
text:
Who is this workshop aimed at?

Postgraduate students in ecology, zoology, conservation biology, statistics, mathematics, data science, and related fields
Quantitative ecologists and wildlife researchers
Wildlife telemetry and tracking practitioners
Conservation NGOs and protected area managers

title: Resources & Literature
text:
This page provides links to official package documentation and software repositories, alongside a curated bibliography of foundational and recent literature across movement ecology modeling topics.

📦 R Packages & Tutorials🌍 Geospatial Data Sources🧠 Behavioural State Estimation🗺️ Space-Use & Home Range🌲 Resource & Step Selection (RSF / SSF / iSSF)🤖 Bayesian & Machine Learning Directions



Behavioural State Estimation

aniMotum: Package Website | GitHub Repository
momentuHMM: Package Vignette & Manual | GitHub Repository
bayesmove: Package Website | GitHub Repository



Space-Use & Telemetry Processing

amt (Animal Movement Tools): Package Documentation | GitHub Repository
ctmm (Continuous-Time Movement Modeling): Package Vignettes | GitHub Repository
move / move2: Package Website | Move2 Documentation



Geospatial Data Processing

rsi (Remote Sensing Integration): Package Documentation

elevatr: Package Vignette
terra: Package Documentation | GitHub Repository
sf: Package Documentation | GitHub Repository
tidyterra: Package Documentation | GitHub Repository
Tutorial for working with Google Earth Engine (GEE)





General Data Sources

STAC Index: Platform for searching through numerous STAC catalogs of available data in the cloud.
Google Earth Engine: A planetary-scale platform for Earth science data and analysis. Provides ability to process remote sensing products in the cloud without need for having powerful computer.
Source Cooperative: Source is a nonprofit data publishing utility built on commodity cloud object storage. Researchers publish data at any scale without running servers, building portals, or writing APIs. Data are available in multiple formats.
NASA Earthdata: Provides large suite of data products from related NASA satellite missions and tools to view and download these data. AppEEARS offers a simple and efficient way to perform data access and transformation processes.
Microsoft Planetary Computer: Provides large catalog of multi-petabyte Earth observation data from a wide variety of products. Provides nice data viewer and data are readily available from their STAC catalog.



Political & Administrative Boundaries

Natural Earth Data: Global country and state/province boundary vectors. Accessed via rnaturalearth.
geoBoundaries Data: High-resolution administrative boundary layers (ADM0–ADM5). Accessed via rgeoboundaries.



Water Extent & Recurrence

JRC Global Surface Water: Global surface water products from the European Commission Joint Research Centre, based on Landsat 5, 7, and 8 imagery. Layers in this collection describe the occurrence, change, and seasonality of surface water from 1984-2021. Data available via STAC catalog and Google Earth Engine.



Elevation & Topography

AWS Terrain Tiles / USGS DEM: Global digital elevation models accessed at varying zoom levels via elevatr. Derived metrics (slope, aspect, terrain ruggedness index [TRI]) calculated using terra::terrain().



OpenStreetMap (Vector Hydrology & Infrastructure)

OpenStreetMap (OSM): Open-access global vector features (water bodies, rivers, roads, buildings). Queried directly via osmdata.



Human Pressure & Population Grids (Cloud COGs)

Global Terrestrial Human Footprint (HFP-100 v1.2): 100 m resolution cumulative human pressure map (2021). Streamed as a Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) from Source Cooperative.
GHS-POP (Global Human Settlement Layer): 100 m modeled residential population estimates (2020). Streamed as a COG from Source Cooperative (cboettig/population).



Land Use / Land Cover (LULC)

ESA WorldCover (10 m): High-resolution global land cover product with 11 classes (2020/2021). Queried via SpatioTemporal Asset Catalog (STAC) through Microsoft Planetary Computer, AWS, or WorldCover website.
Blog comparing different LULC products based on this recent paper.



Multispectral Satellite Imagery

Sentinel-2A Optical Imagery (10 m): Global multi-spectral imagery available at 5-day revisit rates (2017 - present). Available across multiple platforms, such as STAC Catalogs, Copernicus Data Browser, and Google Earth Engine.
Landsat (30 m; multiple missions): Global multi-spectral imagery available at 16-day revisit rates (1972 - present). Available across multiple platforms, such as STAC Catalogs, USGS EarthExplorer, and Google Earth Engine
Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLS; 30 m): The combined measurement across both remote sensing products enables global observations of the land every 2-3 days (2015 - present) and is available from major data sources such as STAC and Google Earth Engine.





Method and Time Step Comparison

title: Preparing for the Workshop
text: This workshop assumes a working knowledge of R and RStudio (or Positron / VS Code). Please complete the installation steps below before attending Day 1 to ensure all required packages and system toolchains are working properly.

title: Preparing for the Workshop
text:
Automated R Package Installation
Copy and paste the code chunk below directly into your R console. This script automatically checks for missing packages, installs standard versions from CRAN, and pulls bleeding-edge versions from R-Universe or GitHub.
# ==============================================================================
# Workshop Package Installer
# Advanced Animal Movement Modelling Training Workshop (2026)
# ==============================================================================

# 1. Install package managers if missing
if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("remotes")
if (!requireNamespace("pak", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("pak")

# 2. Standard CRAN Packages
cran_pkgs <- c(
  # Session 1: Foundations & Data Wrangling
  "tidyverse", "readxl", "plotly", "bayesmove", "shinythemes", 
  "viridis", "rnaturalearth", "scico", "amt",
  
  # Session 2: Space Use & Movement
  "terra", "tidyterra", "tictoc", "units", "move", "ctmm", 
  "progressr", "furrr",
  
  # Session 3: Behavioural State Estimation
  "ggforce", "optimx", "car", "future.apply", "doFuture", "mitools",
  
  # Session 4: Remote Sensing & Earth Observation
  "rsi", "rstac", "osmdata", "elevatr",
  
  # Session 5: Species-Habitat Associations & SSFs
  "lwgeom", "mgcv", "gratia"
)

# Install missing CRAN packages
missing_cran <- cran_pkgs[!(cran_pkgs %in% installed.packages()[, "Package"])]
if (length(missing_cran) > 0) {
  message("Installing missing CRAN packages: ", paste(missing_cran, collapse = ", "))
  install.packages(missing_cran)
}

# 3. Special Repositories (R-Universe & GitHub)

# High-resolution maps (rOpenSci R-Universe)
if (!requireNamespace("rnaturalearthhires", quietly = TRUE)) {
  message("Installing rnaturalearthhires...")
  install.packages("rnaturalearthhires", repos = "[https://ropensci.r-universe.dev](https://ropensci.r-universe.dev)", type = "source")
}

# aniMotum (Ian Jonsen R-Universe)
message("Installing latest aniMotum from R-Universe...")
install.packages(
  "aniMotum", 
  repos = c("[https://ianjonsen.r-universe.dev](https://ianjonsen.r-universe.dev)", "[https://cloud.r-project.org](https://cloud.r-project.org)"),
  dependencies = TRUE
)

# momentuHMM v2.0.0 (GitHub)
message("Installing momentuHMM (v2.0.0) from GitHub...")
remotes::install_github("bmcclintock/momentuHMM", dependencies = TRUE)

# 4. Verification Check
message("\n--- Installation Verification ---")
all_pkgs <- c(cran_pkgs, "rnaturalearthhires", "aniMotum", "momentuHMM")
installed <- all_pkgs %in% installed.packages()[, "Package"]

if (all(installed)) {
  message("✅ All workshop packages are successfully installed!")
} else {
  warning("⚠️ The following packages failed to install: ", 
          paste(all_pkgs[!installed], collapse = ", "))
}
